name: Glute bridge
movement: hips lifted to a line and lowered

phone.placement: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to where you will be.

words.hint: Phone on its side on the floor, side on to you, lying down with your knees bent and feet flat.
words.start: Lay the phone on its side on the floor. I will wait while you get set up: lie down side on to it, knees bent.
words.position: Lie on your back, side on to the phone, knees bent, feet flat on the floor, arms by your sides.
words.top: Hips lifted until knees, hips and shoulders make one straight line, no higher, heels and toes down, knees over the feet.
howto: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width, heels about a hand from your hips, arms by your sides.
Squeeze the buttocks, press through the heels and lift the hips until knees, hips and shoulders make one straight line. No higher — past the line the lower back arches.
Hold at the top for the count, heels and toes down, knees in line with the feet.
Lower slowly — the rep counts when the hips are back on the floor.
words.cannot: Whether the buttocks or the lower back are doing the work, the knees falling in or out (toward the camera) and the pelvis dropping on one side: it sees the line from knees to shoulders, the feet and where they are. If the back pinches, stop.
words.about: Glute bridge — lying on your back side on, knees bent, feet flat, phone on its side: the hips lifted until the hip angle between knee and shoulder is at least 160° at the top, and no more than 8° above the straight line from the knees to the shoulders — past it the lower back arches; the feet, judged at rest between reps, where they can be moved: the shin's angle at the heel between toe and knee 85–122° (more is the feet too far out, and the hamstrings take over); and the feet flat, the heel-to-toe line within 12° of where it was at the start, which also takes off the model's own slant. A rep is under way once the hip angle passes 150° and counts when it is back under 140°. Hold three seconds at the top, lower slowly.
words.lost: Lie down side on to the camera, whole body in
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: Stop if the lower back pinches. The lift comes from the glutes, not from arching the back.
words.easier: A smaller lift; a shorter hold at the top.
words.harder: A weight across the hips; a longer hold; one leg at a time.
words.mistakes: Pushing the hips past the line and arching the lower back; heels or toes lifting; feet too far out (the hamstrings cramp); knees falling in or out.

measurements.label: toe, heel, knee
measurements.why: The shin against the foot, at the heel, judged at rest between reps, where the feet can be moved: about 105–115 with the heels a hand from the hips, past 122 with them half a metre out (the hamstrings take over and cramp), under 85 only with the heels under the hips.

measurements.label: knee, hip, shoulder

settings.label: Hip angle at the top, at least

measurements.why: The angle at the hip between the knee and the shoulder, read on past straight: 180 is one line from the knees to the shoulders, more is the hip pushed above it, so the reading keeps rising as the hips go past the line instead of turning back. Also the progress measurement: under way past 150, down under 140.

measurements.label: hips over the line

settings.label: Hips above the knee-to-shoulder line, at most (degrees)

measurements.why: How far the hip sits off the straight line from the knee to the shoulder, signed: 0 is one line, + the hip pushed above it (the lower back arching to make height), − short of it. About −45 lying down; a correct top reads within a few degrees of 0 (real photos: −3).

measurements.label: foot off the floor

settings.label: Foot off the floor, at most

measurements.why: The heel against the toe, as the change since the start: + the heel lifting, − the toes. Read against the start, so the model's own slant of a flat foot (about nine degrees toe-up) is taken off by itself.

faults.label: Heels lifting
faults.deep: Heels down — they are coming off the floor

faults.label: Toes lifting
faults.deep: Toes down — they are coming off the floor

faults.label: Feet too far out
faults.deep: Walk your feet in toward you — they are well out

faults.label: Feet too close
faults.text: Walk your feet out a little
faults.deep: Walk your feet out — your knees are out over your toes

faults.label: Hips too high
faults.text: Not so high — stop at one line, knees to shoulders
faults.deep: Lower the hips a little — the back is arching

faults.label: Hips short of the line
faults.deep: Higher — knees, hips and shoulders in one line

settings.label: Hip angle that counts as lifted
